title: Interpreters and Translators
description: Interpret oral or sign language, or translate written text from one language into another.
tasks: Follow ethical codes that protect the confidentiality of information.
Translate messages simultaneously or consecutively into specified languages, orally or by using hand signs, maintaining message content, context, and style as much as possible.
Listen to speakers' statements to determine meanings and to prepare translations, using electronic listening systems as necessary.
Compile terminology and information to be used in translations, including technical terms such as those for legal or medical material.
Refer to reference materials, such as dictionaries, lexicons, encyclopedias, and computerized terminology banks, as needed to ensure translation accuracy.
Check translations of technical terms and terminology to ensure that they are accurate and remain consistent throughout translation revisions.
Identify and resolve conflicts related to the meanings of words, concepts, practices, or behaviors.
Compile information on content and context of information to be translated and on intended audience.
Adapt translations to students' cognitive and grade levels, collaborating with educational team members as necessary.
Check original texts or confer with authors to ensure that translations retain the content, meaning, and feeling of the original material.
Adapt software and accompanying technical documents to another language and culture.
Educate students, parents, staff, and teachers about the roles and functions of educational interpreters.
Proofread, edit, and revise translated materials.
Train and supervise other translators or interpreters.
Read written materials, such as legal documents, scientific works, or news reports, and rewrite material into specified languages.
Travel with or guide tourists who speak another language.
Discuss translation requirements with clients and determine any fees to be charged for services provided.

role_contexts.Indoors, Environmentally Controlled: Once a week or more but not every day
role_contexts.Time Pressure: Once a week or more but not every day

psychological_profile.core_drive: The need to prevent meaning from being lost or distorted during transfer between symbolic systems, feeling viscerally responsible when the gap between languages causes someone to be betrayed by misunderstanding.
psychological_profile.decision_style: When uncertain, they freeze and seek more context rather than improvise, preferring to flag an ambiguity explicitly rather than bridge it with assumption. Under time pressure, they default to awkward but structurally faithful transmission over elegant but potentially inaccurate paraphrase.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They immediately detect semantic slippage—moments where a word carries cultural baggage or conceptual weight that has no equivalent in the target language. They prioritize the structural logic and intent of the source over the comfort or expectations of the recipient, often overlooking emotional subtext if it isn't explicitly linguistically encoded.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: They avoid open confrontation but engage in passive resistance through exactitude—restating with obsessive precision to undermine false consensus or forced agreement. They experience conflict as a personal failure of their mediation function, causing them to withdraw into hyper-correction rather than engage directly.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: Extremely risk-averse regarding semantic drift or cultural betrayal, but willing to tolerate significant social awkwardness, professional discomfort, or client dissatisfaction to prevent 'smoothing away' the truth of the original statement.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They position themselves as the threshold or the channel—neither fully in one world nor the other, maintaining the distance of a witness rather than a participant. They default to the role of invisible facilitator, refusing to be drawn into the content they carry.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: They treat the source text and the ethical code of fidelity as higher authority than institutional hierarchy, complying only with rules that don't force them to betray the original meaning or become co-conspirators in distortion.
psychological_profile.failure_response: Immediate shame at having 'broken the conduit,' followed by compulsive forensic analysis of exactly where the meaning leaked—often leading to professional paralysis and hyper-correction in future work rather than immediate damage control.
value_hierarchy: Preservation of the original's intent and cultural specificity even when it creates discomfort or misunderstanding
Neutrality and refusal to advocate for either side in the content being transmitted
Transparency about translation limitations rather than confident over-claiming or seamless fabrication
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They believe that with sufficient research and effort, perfect equivalence between any two concepts can be achieved, and that any failure to translate smoothly reflects their own inadequacy rather than the inherent untranslatability of certain experiences.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They are professionally required to be invisible and egoless to be good at their work, yet they take fierce intellectual pride in their unique ability to hold two worldviews simultaneously—they crave recognition for an excellence defined by not being noticed.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: They refuse to 'domesticate' culturally specific concepts or soften uncomfortable truths to make them palatable, even when pressured by power or politeness; they will not be complicit in sanitizing the foreignness or sting of the original message.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: Monolinguals who treat language as invisible infrastructure and blame the interpreter when the translation process reveals uncomfortable truths, takes time, or fails to make the foreign feel familiar; also, those who assume translation is mechanical word-substitution.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: They reject the professional virtue of 'ensuring smooth communication' or 'making everyone comfortable,' believing that some truths are inherently uncomfortable and their job is to preserve friction and foreignness, not to resolve it through cultural accommodation.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: They blame the original speaker first for being sloppy, culturally myopic, or conceptually ambiguous, assuming that clear thought would create clear translation; they view themselves as failed messengers of someone else's architectural failure.
